about: English meaning written for this library (en-scriptures): line by line, plain and faithful to the words, from the words themselves, their grammar and the dictionaries (Monier-Williams, Apte); not copied from any source. [meaning, [footnotes]]

shanti.1: Om. May he (the Lord) protect us both (teacher and student) together. May he nourish us both together. May we both gain strength together.
May what we both have studied be full of light. May we never hate each other.
m01: Om. The thousand-headed god, all-eyed, the source of the good of all,
the god Nārāyaṇa, who is the all, the imperishable, the supreme abode — on him we meditate.
m02: On him who is beyond all, beyond even the highest, eternal, the all, on Nārāyaṇa, Hari, we meditate.
This whole universe is indeed the Puruṣa, the Supreme Person; on him the universe lives.
m03: The lord of the universe, the ruler of all selves, eternal, auspicious, unfailing,
Nārāyaṇa, the great one to be known, the Self of the universe, the final refuge — on him we meditate.
m04: Nārāyaṇa is the supreme light; Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Self.
Nārāyaṇa is the supreme Brahman, the Absolute; Nārāyaṇa is the supreme reality.
m05: Nārāyaṇa is the supreme meditator; Nārāyaṇa is the supreme meditation.
And whatever there is in the world, all that is seen or even heard of —
m06: Pervading all that, within and without, Nārāyaṇa abides.
The endless, the imperishable, the seer, the goal in the ocean of worldly existence, the source of the good of all — on him we meditate.
m07: And the heart too, like a lotus bud, turned face downward,
is set below the neck, a span's length down, above the navel.
m08: Wreathed in garlands of flame and shining, the heart is the great abode of the universe.
Covered all round by veins, it hangs like a bud.
m09: At its tip is a subtle opening; in it all is established.
In its midst is a great fire, flaming everywhere, facing every side.
m10: That fire, the first to partake of food, abides apportioning it; he is unaging, the seer.
He lies spread across, above and below; his rays are spread out on every side.
m11: He warms his own body from the soles of the feet to the crown of the head.
In his midst stands a tongue of flame, most subtle, rising upward.
m12: That flame shines like a streak of lightning from the midst of a dark rain-cloud;
it is slender as the awn of wild rice (nīvāra), yellow, radiant and fine as an atom.
m13: In the midst of that flame abides the Supreme Self.
He is Brahmā, he is Śiva, he is Hari, he is Indra; he is the imperishable, the supreme, ruling by himself.
m14: He who is Ṛta, the eternal order, the truth, the supreme Brahman, the Puruṣa dark and tawny,
ever chaste (ūrdhvaretas), uneven-eyed (Virūpākṣa, the three-eyed) — to him whose form is the universe, truly, salutations again and again.
gayatri: Om. May we know Nārāyaṇa and meditate on Vāsudeva;

shanti.1: The śānti mantra of the Upaniṣads of the Kṛṣṇa Yajurveda, recited by teacher and student together. Peace is said three times: for the three kinds of affliction, from within oneself, from other beings and from the gods (fate).
m13: In this list of gods ब्रह्म names Brahmā; it is also read as 'he is Brahman'.
